name: Johannes Gutenberg
description: Mainz goldsmith who combined movable metal type, oil-based ink, and a screw press into a printing system around 1450. The resulting collapse in the cost of texts — beginning with his 42-line Bible — accelerated the Renaissance, Reformation, and Scientific Revolution.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
description: Florentine painter, engineer, and anatomist — the archetypal Renaissance polymath. Painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper while filling thousands of notebook pages with studies of anatomy, water, flight, and machines centuries ahead of fabrication.

name: Christopher Columbus
description: Genoese navigator whose 1492 Atlantic crossing under Castilian sponsorship opened sustained contact between Eurasia and the Americas — initiating the Columbian Exchange of crops, peoples, and diseases, and the era of European colonization with its devastating consequences for indigenous populations.

name: Martin Luther
description: German friar whose Ninety-five Theses (1517) against indulgences ignited the Protestant Reformation. His doctrine of justification by faith, vernacular Bible translation, and defiance at Worms fractured Latin Christendom permanently.

name: Suleiman the Magnificent
description: Longest-reigning Ottoman sultan, under whom the empire reached its zenith — taking Belgrade, Rhodes, and most of Hungary, besieging Vienna, reforming law (hence 'Kanuni', the Lawgiver), and patronizing a golden age of Ottoman architecture under Sinan.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
description: Polish canon and astronomer whose De revolutionibus (1543) placed the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the cosmos — the pivot of the Scientific Revolution, published as he lay dying.
